pairs.question: Quis est iste rex gloriae?
pairs.derivation: Verbatim Psalm 23,10 quoted by Isidore to gloss 'Sabaoth'. The quoted verse itself is a genuine interrogative ('Who is this king of glory?') immediately answered ('The Lord of hosts'). Stripped the section marker [7], the scriptural-citation framing 'de quo in Psalmo ab angelis dicitur (23,10):' and the enclosing quotation marks. Nothing omitted between question and answer; the answer is the entire reply.

pairs.question: Deus autem, qui non est factus, quomodo est perfectus?
pairs.answer: Sed hoc vocabulum de usu nostro sumpsit humana inopia, sicut et reliqua verba, quatenus id quod ineffabile est utcumque dici possit, quoniam de Deo nihil digne humanus sermo dicit, sicut sunt et alia.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question: having noted 'perfectio' implies completion of something made, Isidore asks how God, who was not made, can be called perfect. Kept the preceding clause 'Deus autem, qui non est factus' so 'perfectus' has its subject. The answer is the operative reply opening section [32] ('but human poverty took this word from our usage...'); ran to its full stop. Stripped section markers [31] and [32].
